Index: README.md =================================================================== --- README.md +++ README.md @@ -1,243 +1,281 @@ # Mosque Management System (MMS)

A modern, production-ready mosque management platform that combines a public-facing community website with a secure, role-based admin dashboard for managing operations, funding, events, and community members. Built for mosques and Islamic centers that need a single system to manage worship services, financial records, communication, and administration from one place. ## Live Demo [![Live Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Live-Demo-22c55e?style=for-the-badge&logo=vercel&logoColor=white)](https://alnoormosque.vercel.app/) ## Screenshots

## Project Highlights
🏛️ Community Platform
Public website for mosque updates, prayer times, and announcements		 💰 Finance Tracking
Donation, expense, fund, and income management with reporting
👥 Member Management
Members, staff, committee, roles, and permission controls		 📊 Operational Insights
Reports, activity logs, and admin dashboards for decision making
## Why MMS? - Manage mosque operations from a single dashboard - Keep public content updated with announcements, prayer times, and events - Track donations, expenses, and funds with financial transparency - Handle members, staff, committee roles, and permissions cleanly - Maintain a professional digital presence for the community --- ## Features ### Public Website - Homepage with prayer times and next prayer countdown - Events and announcement sections - Khutbah archive and community content pages - Committee and gallery pages - Donation page with Bangladeshi Taka support - Contact page and public inquiry handling - SEO metadata, sitemap, robots configuration, and manifest support ### Admin Dashboard - Donation, income, expense, and balance overview - Charts for donation trends and fund allocation - Roles and permissions management - Members, committee, staff, and user controls - Prayer time management and operational records - Assets, maintenance, documents, and request workflows - Ramadan, audit logs, and settings modules +### Event Contribution Tracking + +An event can be linked to an existing donation fund and given a per-head contribution amount. +Members are then assigned to the event, and the linked fund's approved payments drive everything +on the event's contribution page (`/admin/events/`): + +``` +Approved Fund Contribution → donations.member_id identifies the member + → paid / remaining derived at render time + → Completed / Incomplete derived (paid >= assigned) + → summary counts and progress bar follow automatically +``` + +- Per-member assigned, paid, remaining, and Completed/Incomplete status +- Search, status and payment-stage filters, sorting, and pagination +- Email reminders to one member at a time, with history of what was sent and when +- No second payment system: approving a donation in `/admin/donations` is all it takes + ### Security & Access Control - Supabase authentication integration - Role-based access control (RBAC) - Permission checks enforced in logic and database policy layers - Secure server/client separation for sensitive operations --- ## Tech Stack | Layer | Technology | | --- | --- | | Frontend | Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript | | Styling | Tailwind CSS v4 | | UI Components | Radix UI, Lucide React | | Forms | React Hook Form, Zod | | Data Tables | TanStack Table | | Charts | Recharts | | Backend | Supabase (PostgreSQL, Auth, Storage, RLS) | | Notifications | Sonner | | Utilities | clsx, tailwind-merge, date-fns | --- ## Project Structure ```bash . ├── src/ │ ├── app/ │ │ ├── (public)/ # public-facing pages │ │ ├── (auth)/ # login and auth flows │ │ ├── admin/ # protected admin dashboard │ │ ├── api/ # API routes │ │ └── auth/ # OAuth/callback routes │ ├── components/ │ │ ├── admin/ # dashboard and admin UI │ │ ├── forms/ # reusable form components │ │ ├── public/ # public-facing UI │ │ └── ui/ # shadcn-style primitives │ ├── lib/ │ │ ├── actions/ # server actions │ │ ├── auth/ # auth helpers │ │ ├── queries/ # data fetchers │ │ ├── permissions/ # RBAC rules │ │ ├── supabase/ # Supabase clients │ │ ├── utils/ # formatting and helpers │ │ ├── validations/ # Zod schemas │ │ └── prayer-times.ts # time-related logic │ ├── constants/ │ ├── types/ │ └── proxy.ts # proxy/middleware replacement for Next 16 ├── supabase/ │ ├── migrations/ │ └── seed.sql ├── public/ ├── package.json ├── next.config.ts ├── tsconfig.json ├── eslint.config.mjs ├── README.md └── .env.example ``` --- ## Getting Started ### Prerequisites - Node.js 18.18+ (recommended: Node 20 LTS) - A Supabase project - A configured local environment for development ### Installation ```bash npm install ``` ### Run the app ```bash npm run dev ``` Then open: ```text http://localhost:3000 ``` --- ## Environment Variables Create a `.env.local` file in the project root using the following values: ```env NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=https://your-project.supabase.co NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=your-anon-key SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=your-service-role-key NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=http://localhost:3000 ``` ### Variable Notes - `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`: Your Supabase project URL - `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`: Public anon key for browser access - `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`: Server-side secret; keep it private - `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`: Base URL used by the app in local or production environments +### Email (Event Contribution Reminders) + +Reminders are sent from the server with Nodemailer over SMTP. These variables are optional: +without them the contribution tracking page still works, it just reports that reminders are +disabled and the send button stays unavailable. + +```env +SMTP_HOST=smtp.example.com +SMTP_PORT=587 +SMTP_USER=your-smtp-username +SMTP_PASS=your-smtp-password +SMTP_SECURE=false +EMAIL_FROM=admin@your-mosque.com +EMAIL_FROM_NAME=Al-Noor Mosque +``` + +- `SMTP_PORT`: `587` for STARTTLS, `465` for implicit TLS (`SMTP_SECURE=true` is applied automatically on 465) +- `EMAIL_FROM`: must be an address the provider accepts as a verified sender. It always falls back to `SMTP_USER` if omitted, and can never be set from the browser +- These values are read only in `src/lib/email.ts`, which is a `server-only` module, so credentials never reach client code + --- ## Database Setup Apply the database schema and policies from the Supabase migrations. ```bash # If you use the Supabase CLI supabase db push ``` Or import the SQL files manually from the `supabase/migrations/` directory in the Supabase SQL editor. Then seed initial data using: ```bash supabase/seed.sql ``` This file contains initial records such as roles, funds, and default system data. For the first admin user, create the account in the Supabase Auth dashboard and update the corresponding profile record to assign the appropriate role, such as `super_admin`. --- ## Available Scripts ```bash npm run dev # start development server npm run build # production build npm run start # run production build npm run lint # run ESLint ``` --- ## Notes - Currency is handled in Bangladeshi Taka (`৳`) - The donation flow is designed for manual payment tracking rather than a third-party payment gateway - This project uses modern Next.js conventions; in Next 16, the role of middleware is handled through the app proxy setup in `src/proxy.ts` --- ## Contributing Contributions are welcome. If you want to improve the application, please open an issue or submit a pull request with a clear description of the change. --- ## Project Status This project is under active development and is designed for mosque administration workflows, community engagement, and operational reporting.

--- supabase/migrations/009_event_contributions.sql	
+++ supabase/migrations/009_event_contributions.sql	
@@ -0,0 +1,110 @@
+-- ============================================================
+-- EVENT CONTRIBUTION TRACKING
+-- ============================================================
+-- `events.fund_id`, `events.contribution_*`, `event_members` and
+-- `contribution_reminder_emails` were appended to 001 after that migration had
+-- already been applied to live databases, so an existing project would never
+-- pick them up through the normal migration chain. Everything below is
+-- idempotent: it is a no-op on a fresh install (001 already created the
+-- objects) and creates whatever is missing everywhere else.
+--
+-- Design note: no duplicate money is stored here. `event_members.assigned_amount`
+-- is the only new amount, and it is a target, not a ledger. Collected totals,
+-- paid amounts and Completed/Incomplete status are always derived from approved
+-- `donations` rows (status = 'completed') that carry `donations.member_id`.
+
+-- ============================================================
+-- COLUMNS
+-- ============================================================
+
+ALTER TABLE events
+  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS fund_id UUID REFERENCES donation_funds(id) ON DELETE SET NULL;
+
+ALTER TABLE events
+  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS contribution_amount NUMERIC(12,2) DEFAULT 0;
+
+ALTER TABLE events
+  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS contribution_start_date DATE;
+
+ALTER TABLE events
+  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS contribution_due_date DATE;
+
+-- ============================================================
+-- TABLES
+-- ============================================================
+
+CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS event_members (
+  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuid_generate_v4(),
+  event_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES events(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
+  member_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES members(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
+  assigned_amount NUMERIC(12,2) DEFAULT 0,
+  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
+  created_by UUID REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
+  UNIQUE (event_id, member_id)
+);
+
+CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS contribution_reminder_emails (
+  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuid_generate_v4(),
+  event_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES events(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
+  member_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES members(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
+  recipient_email TEXT NOT NULL,
+  subject TEXT NOT NULL,
+  message TEXT NOT NULL,
+  sent_by UUID REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
+  sent_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
+  status VARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'sent' CHECK (status IN ('sent','failed'))
+);
+
+-- `donations.member_id` is the link that makes payment -> member matching a
+-- foreign key lookup instead of name/email/phone string guessing (003 added
+-- `members.user_id`). Backfill the gap for donations that carry a `user_id` but
+-- no `member_id`, matching on that account link only -- never on a name. The
+-- correlated subquery keeps this to one row per donation even if a user somehow
+-- owns several member records.
+UPDATE donations d
+SET member_id = (
+  SELECT m.id
+  FROM members m
+  WHERE m.user_id = d.user_id
+  ORDER BY m.created_at
+  LIMIT 1
+)
+WHERE d.member_id IS NULL
+  AND d.user_id IS NOT NULL
+  AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM members m WHERE m.user_id = d.user_id);
+
+-- ============================================================
+-- INDEXES
+-- ============================================================
+
+CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_event_members_event_id ON event_members(event_id);
+CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_event_members_member_id ON event_members(member_id);
+CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_contribution_reminder_emails_event_id
+  ON contribution_reminder_emails(event_id);
+CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_contribution_reminder_emails_member_id
+  ON contribution_reminder_emails(member_id);
+CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_events_fund_id ON events(fund_id);
+
+-- ============================================================
+-- ROW LEVEL SECURITY
+-- ============================================================
+-- These two tables were created without RLS in 001, which left them readable by
+-- any client holding the anon key. Members' names, phones, emails and the full
+-- reminder history all live here, so both are locked down behind `event.manage`.
+
+ALTER TABLE event_members ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
+ALTER TABLE contribution_reminder_emails ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
+
+DROP POLICY IF EXISTS event_members_admin_all ON event_members;
+CREATE POLICY event_members_admin_all ON event_members
+  FOR ALL
+  USING (public.has_permission('event.manage') OR public.current_user_role() = 'super_admin')
+  WITH CHECK (public.has_permission('event.manage') OR public.current_user_role() = 'super_admin');
+
+DROP POLICY IF EXISTS contribution_reminder_emails_admin_all ON contribution_reminder_emails;
+CREATE POLICY contribution_reminder_emails_admin_all ON contribution_reminder_emails
+  FOR ALL
+  USING (public.has_permission('event.manage') OR public.current_user_role() = 'super_admin')
+  WITH CHECK (public.has_permission('event.manage') OR public.current_user_role() = 'super_admin');
+
+-- No public read policy on purpose: contribution status is financial member data.
\ No newline at end of file

parts.text:
# TASK: Add Event Contribution Tracking + Member Payment Status + Email Reminder System

I already have a fully working Mosjid Management System.

IMPORTANT:
- Do NOT rebuild the project.
- Do NOT rewrite the existing Fund module.
- Do NOT change existing working fund collection/approval logic unnecessarily.
- First inspect the current Event, Fund, Member, Donation/Transaction, Authentication, Database, and Admin UI implementation.
- Extend the existing system cleanly.

The goal is to add a new Event Contribution Tracking feature on top of the existing system.

---

# EXISTING WORKFLOW

The project already supports:

- Creating Funds from Admin Panel
- Setting Fund name
- Setting target amount
- Fund progress percentage
- Receiving money manually
- Approving received fund contributions
- Approved amount automatically increasing Fund collected amount
- Member management
- Events
- Admin authentication

Example existing use case:

Event/Fund:
"Tarabir Hadiya"

Total participants:
500 members

Contribution per member:
৳520

Expected total:

500 × ৳520 = ৳260,000

Initially:

Collected:
৳0

Progress:
0%

When members start paying, Admin receives/approves their payments and the existing fund progress increases.

DO NOT break this existing workflow.

---

# NEW FEATURE GOAL

After creating an event, Admin should be able to click the event and open a dedicated Event Details / Contribution Tracking page.

This page should show:

1. Event information
2. Linked Fund information
3. Overall collection progress
4. All assigned members
5. Contribution amount per member
6. Individual member payment status
7. Paid amount
8. Remaining amount
9. Email reminder action
10. Collection statistics

The page should update automatically according to approved Fund payments.

---

# 1. EVENT + FUND RELATIONSHIP

Allow an Event to be connected to an existing Fund.

During Event creation or editing, provide:

Linked Fund:
[ Select Fund ]

Example:

Event:
Tarabir Hadiya

Linked Fund:
Tarabir Hadiya Fund

Per Head Contribution:
৳520

The Event must NOT maintain a separate conflicting collected amount.

The existing Fund data must remain the financial source of truth.

---

# 2. EVENT CONTRIBUTION SETTINGS

Add contribution-related settings to Event.

Fields:

- Event Name
- Event Description
- Event Date
- Linked Fund
- Per Head Contribution Amount
- Assigned Members
- Contribution Start Date
- Contribution Due Date
- Status

Example:

Event Name:
Tarabir Hadiya

Linked Fund:
Tarabir Hadiya Fund

Per Head:
৳520

Assigned Members:
500

Expected Collection:
৳260,000

Expected Collection should be calculated automatically:

assigned member count × per-head amount

Do NOT require Admin to manually calculate this value.

---

# 3. MEMBER ASSIGNMENT

Admin must be able to assign members to the Event.

Use the existing Member database.

Provide:

[ Add Members ]

Admin should be able to:

- Select all members
- Select individual members
- Search members
- Filter members
- Add multiple members
- Remove a member from the event if necessary

Do NOT duplicate member personal data.

Store member references using member IDs.

---

# 4. EVENT DETAILS PAGE

When Admin clicks an Event from the Events list, open a dedicated details page.

Use the existing project route structure.

Prefer something similar to:

/admin/events/[eventId]

Do not force this route if the existing architecture uses another convention.

---

# 5. EVENT DETAILS HEADER

At the top show:

Event Name

Example:

Tarabir Hadiya

Then show:

Event Date
Contribution Due Date
Linked Fund
Per Head Contribution
Assigned Members
Completed Members
Incomplete Members

---

# 6. SUMMARY CARDS

Create clean summary cards.

Example:

---------------------------------

Target Collection
৳260,000

---------------------------------

Collected
৳104,000

---------------------------------

Remaining
৳156,000

---------------------------------

Completed
200 / 500 Members

---------------------------------

Also show:

Collection Progress

████████░░░░ 40%

Progress must come from approved payments only.

---

# 7. MEMBER CONTRIBUTION TABLE

Create the main contribution tracking table.

Columns:

Member
Phone
Email
Assigned Amount
Paid Amount
Remaining
Status
Actions

Example:

| Member | Assigned | Paid | Remaining | Status | Action |
|--------|----------|------|-----------|--------|--------|
| Rahim | ৳520 | ৳520 | ৳0 | Completed | Email |
| Karim | ৳520 | ৳0 | ৳520 | Incomplete | Email |
| Hasan | ৳520 | ৳300 | ৳220 | Incomplete | Email |

---

# 8. PAYMENT STATUS LOGIC

The status must be calculated automatically.

Use ONLY approved payments.

For each event member:

approvedPaidAmount =
sum of approved contributions from that member to the Event's linked Fund

Then:

If:

approvedPaidAmount >= assignedContributionAmount

Status:

Completed

Otherwise:

Status:

Incomplete

Do NOT manually toggle Completed/Incomplete.

Payment approval should be the source of truth.

---

# 9. PARTIAL PAYMENT SUPPORT

Support partial payments.

Example:

Per Head:
৳520

Member paid:
৳300

Show:

Paid:
৳300

Remaining:
৳220

Status:
Incomplete

If later another approved payment of ৳220 is received:

Paid:
৳520

Remaining:
৳0

Status automatically changes to:

Completed

---

# 10. OVERPAYMENT

If a member pays more than the required contribution:

Example:

Required:
৳520

Paid:
৳600

Show:

Paid:
৳600

Remaining:
৳0

Status:
Completed

Do not display a negative remaining amount.

Use:

remaining = max(required - paid, 0)

Do not lose the actual paid amount.

---

# 11. MEMBER STATUS BADGES

Use visually clear badges.

Completed:

Green badge

✓ Completed

Incomplete:

Soft orange/red badge

○ Incomplete

Keep styling consistent with the existing Islamic admin dashboard.

Do not introduce excessive colors.

---

# 12. FILTERS

Above the member table add:

Search Member

Status Filter:

- All
- Completed
- Incomplete

Optional filters:

- Paid
- Unpaid
- Partial

The core status must still remain:

Completed / Incomplete

---

# 13. QUICK STATISTICS

Display:

Total Assigned Members

Completed Members

Incomplete Members

Collection Completion %

Example:

500 Total

200 Completed

300 Incomplete

40% Member Completion

This is separate from financial progress.

---

# 14. EMAIL REMINDER ACTION

Each member row should contain a Message/Email icon.

Example:

✉

When Admin clicks the email icon:

Open a small modal/dialog.

---

# 15. EMAIL MODAL

The modal should automatically load member information.

Fields:

To:
member@example.com

This must come automatically from the Member profile.

Do not require Admin to manually type the member email.

Also show:

Member Name
Event Name
Contribution Amount
Paid Amount
Remaining Amount

---

# 16. EMAIL SUBJECT

Auto-generate a useful subject.

Example:

Contribution Reminder - Tarabir Hadiya | Al-Noor Mosque

Allow Admin to edit the subject before sending.

---

# 17. MESSAGE BOX

Provide a message textarea.

Pre-fill it with a professional default message.

Example concept:

Assalamu Alaikum [Member Name],

This is a friendly reminder regarding your contribution for "Tarabir Hadiya" organized by Al-Noor Mosque.

Assigned Contribution: ৳520
Paid: ৳0
Remaining: ৳520
Due Date: [date]

We would appreciate your contribution within the scheduled period.

JazakAllahu Khairan.

Al-Noor Mosque

Admin must be able to edit the message before sending.

---

# 18. EMAIL SEND BUTTON

Modal actions:

Cancel

Send Email

When Admin presses Send Email:

1. Validate member email
2. Send email from the server
3. Disable button during sending
4. Show loading state
5. Prevent accidental duplicate clicks

Never expose mail credentials to browser/client code.

---

# 19. EMAIL DESIGN

Send a properly structured HTML email.

Email should include:

- Al-Noor Mosque logo if available
- Mosque name
- Islamic greeting
- Member name
- Event name
- Assigned contribution
- Paid amount
- Remaining amount
- Due date
- Admin custom message
- Contact/footer section

Use a clean Islamic visual style.

Keep HTML email responsive.

---

# 20. EMAIL SENDER

Use the existing email infrastructure if the project already has one.

FIRST inspect whether the project currently uses:

- Resend
- SMTP
- Nodemailer
- Supabase Edge Functions
- Another mail provider

If an email provider already exists:

Reuse it.

Do NOT introduce another provider unnecessarily.

If no email service exists:

Implement a clean server-side email service abstraction.

Preferred options:

1. Resend
or
2. SMTP/Nodemailer

Configure through environment variables.

Example:

EMAIL_FROM=
EMAIL_FROM_NAME=
RESEND_API_KEY=

OR SMTP configuration if applicable.

Add required variables to:

.env.example

Never commit real credentials.

---

# 21. SENDER ADDRESS

The email should appear from the configured mosque/admin email.

Example:

Al-Noor Mosque
<admin@domain.com>

Do NOT spoof arbitrary sender emails.

Use only a verified/configured sender accepted by the selected email provider.

---

# 22. SEND SUCCESS FEEDBACK

After successful sending:

Close or update the modal.

Show clear success feedback:

✓ Email sent successfully to member@example.com

Use the existing toast/dialog system.

Do not use browser alert().

---

# 23. SEND FAILURE FEEDBACK

If sending fails:

Keep the modal open.

Show:

Unable to send email. Please try again.

Display a useful error without exposing API keys, server internals, or sensitive information.

---

# 24. EMAIL HISTORY

Store reminder email history if reasonably compatible with the current database architecture.

Suggested fields:

id
event_id
member_id
recipient_email
subject
message
sent_by
sent_at
status

Statuses:

sent
failed

This allows Admin to know whether a reminder was already sent.

---

# 25. EMAIL STATUS IN MEMBER ROW

If an email was successfully sent, optionally show small supporting information:

Last reminder:
02 Oct 2026, 8:30 PM

Do not clutter the table.

It can appear inside the row action tooltip, details menu, or member contribution details.

---

# 26. BULK REMINDERS

Do NOT make bulk email sending the main feature in the first implementation.

Focus first on reliable one-member-at-a-time sending.

However, structure the code so a future feature like:

"Send Reminder to All Incomplete Members"

can be added later.

Do NOT automatically send emails without Admin confirmation.

---

# 27. PAYMENT → MEMBER MATCHING

This is extremely important.

The system must reliably identify which member made an approved payment.

Inspect the current Donation/Fund transaction schema.

Use existing member_id if available.

If contributions currently do not store member_id:

Add the minimum safe relationship necessary so an approved Fund contribution can be associated with a Member.

Do NOT rely only on:

- Name matching
- Email text matching
- Phone text matching

Use member ID / foreign key whenever possible.

---

# 28. FUND APPROVAL INTEGRATION

Existing fund approval workflow must remain unchanged.

When Admin approves a contribution:

Existing behavior:

Fund collected amount increases.

New additional behavior:

The Event Contribution page automatically reflects:

- Member Paid Amount
- Remaining Amount
- Completed/Incomplete Status
- Overall completed member count
- Financial progress

No separate manual event payment entry should be required.

---

# 29. EVENT FINANCIAL SOURCE OF TRUTH

Avoid duplicated financial values.

Use:

Approved Fund Contributions

as the financial source of truth.

Event page calculations should derive from those approved contributions.

Do not maintain a separate manually editable:

event_collected_amount

unless the existing architecture absolutely requires it.

---

# 30. TABLE UX

Member contribution table should support:

- Search
- Status filter
- Pagination
- Sorting

Useful sorting:

Name
Assigned Amount
Paid Amount
Remaining Amount
Status

Default layout should remain clean.

---

# 31. MEMBER ROW ACTIONS

Actions may contain:

✉ Send Email

Optional:

View Member

View Payment History

Do NOT overload the row with too many icons.

---

# 32. MEMBER CONTRIBUTION DETAILS

When clicking a member, optionally show a simple contribution detail drawer/modal:

Member:
Rahim

Event:
Tarabir Hadiya

Required:
৳520

Approved Payments:

05 Oct
৳300

12 Oct
৳220

----------------

Total Paid:
৳520

Remaining:
৳0

Status:
Completed

Use existing payment data.

---

# 33. EVENT DETAILS DESIGN

Maintain the existing Al-Noor Mosque UI.

Use:

- Emerald green
- Dark green
- Gold accents
- Warm white
- Clean cards
- Subtle shadows

Do NOT over-design this page.

Information hierarchy:

1. Event title/details
2. Collection progress
3. Member completion statistics
4. Member contribution table

Avoid unnecessary charts.

This page is primarily for tracking collection progress.

---

# 34. RECOMMENDED LAYOUT

Desktop:

-------------------------------------------------------
Tarabir Hadiya

Event Date | Due Date | Linked Fund | Per Head ৳520
-------------------------------------------------------

[ Target ] [ Collected ] [ Remaining ] [ Completed ]

Collection Progress
████████████░░░░ 40%

-------------------------------------------------------

500 Members
200 Completed
300 Incomplete

[ Search Member ] [ Status: All ]

-------------------------------------------------------

Member Contribution Table

-------------------------------------------------------

Mobile:

Stack summary cards.

Make member table responsive.

Use horizontal scrolling or a clean mobile card representation.

---

# 35. DATABASE CHANGES

Before creating new tables, inspect the existing database.

Reuse existing tables whenever possible.

Possible relationships may require:

event_id
fund_id
member_id

If necessary, create a junction table similar to:

event_members

Fields:

id
event_id
member_id
assigned_amount
created_at
created_by

Use the project's existing naming conventions.

Do NOT blindly create this table if an equivalent relationship already exists.

---

# 36. DO NOT STORE DERIVED STATUS UNNECESSARILY

Prefer calculating:

Paid Amount

Remaining

Completed/Incomplete

from real approved contribution data.

Avoid storing values that can easily become inconsistent.

For example:

Completed status should normally be derived:

paid >= assigned_amount

instead of manually storing and updating it.

---

# 37. PER-MEMBER AMOUNT

Event has a default:

Per Head Contribution Amount

Example:

৳520

When members are assigned, use this value as their assigned amount.

If appropriate within the existing architecture, allow Admin to override the assigned amount for an individual member.

Example:

Default:
৳520

Specific Member:
৳1,040

But the default workflow must remain simple.

---

# 38. TARGET AMOUNT RELATION

If this Event Fund is based purely on equal member contribution:

Suggested Expected Amount:

Member Count × Per Head

Example:

500 × 520 = ৳260,000

Show this calculation to Admin.

However, DO NOT unexpectedly overwrite an existing Fund target amount without confirmation.

If Event expected amount differs from existing Fund target:

Show Admin the difference.

Preserve existing Fund data safely.

---

# 39. SECURITY

Respect existing roles and permissions.

Only authorized Admin/Treasurer users should be able to:

- Assign event members
- Send reminders
- View financial member status
- Approve payments

Normal public users must not have access to this Admin Event Contribution page.

Email sending must happen server-side.

---

# 40. AUDIT LOG

If the project already has Audit Logs, integrate:

Track:

- Event member added
- Event member removed
- Reminder email sent
- Contribution approval if already tracked

Reuse existing audit log architecture.

Do NOT build a second audit system.

---

# 41. DO NOT BREAK EXISTING FEATURES

Preserve:

- Fund creation
- Fund target
- Fund approval
- Fund progress
- Events
- Member management
- Donations/payments
- Authentication
- RBAC
- Reports
- Existing UI theme

Make incremental changes only.

---

# 42. IMPLEMENTATION APPROACH

Before coding:

1. Inspect existing project.
2. Locate Event implementation.
3. Locate Fund implementation.
4. Locate Member implementation.
5. Locate payment/donation approval logic.
6. Locate database schema/migrations.
7. Locate auth/RBAC.
8. Check whether email service already exists.

Then create a short implementation plan.

After that, implement the feature using the project's existing architecture.

Do not rewrite unrelated files.

---

# 43. TEST CASE

Use this scenario to verify implementation:

Event:
Tarabir Hadiya

Members:
500

Default contribution:
৳520/member

Expected amount:
৳260,000

Initial:

Collected:
৳0

Completed:
0

Incomplete:
500

Progress:
0%


Member Rahim pays ৳520.

Before approval:

Rahim:
Incomplete

Paid:
৳0 approved


After Admin approves payment:

Rahim:

Paid:
৳520

Remaining:
৳0

Status:
Completed


Event:

Completed:
1 / 500

Collected:
৳520

Progress should update from the linked Fund.


Member Karim pays ৳300 and Admin approves.

Karim:

Paid:
৳300

Remaining:
৳220

Status:
Incomplete


Admin clicks Email icon beside Karim.

Modal opens automatically with:

Karim's email

Event details

Assigned:
৳520

Paid:
৳300

Remaining:
৳220

Admin writes/edits reminder.

Clicks Send.

Email is sent from configured mosque/admin email.

Show:

Email sent successfully.

---

# 44. FINAL ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

The feature is complete only when:

✓ Event can link to a Fund

✓ Event can have a per-head contribution amount

✓ Existing members can be assigned to the Event

✓ Event detail page displays all assigned members

✓ Each member shows assigned amount

✓ Approved Fund payment is linked to correct member

✓ Paid amount updates automatically

✓ Remaining amount updates automatically

✓ Completed status updates automatically

✓ Partial payments work

✓ Event summary counts update automatically

✓ Fund progress remains correct

✓ Email icon exists for each member

✓ Member email auto-fills

✓ Reminder modal works

✓ Admin can edit message

✓ Structured email sends successfully

✓ Success/error feedback works

✓ Email credentials remain server-side

✓ Existing project functionality remains intact

✓ Mobile layout works

✓ No TypeScript/build errors

✓ No unnecessary database duplication

---

# FINAL INSTRUCTION

Implement this as an extension of the existing Event + Fund + Member workflow.

The most important principle is:

Approved Fund Contribution
        ↓
Identify Member
        ↓
Update Event Member Paid Amount
        ↓
Calculate Remaining Amount
        ↓
Automatically determine Completed / Incomplete
        ↓
Update Event Progress and Statistics

Do not create a second independent payment system for Events.

The Event Contribution page must be a tracking and management layer on top of the existing Fund payment system.
I'll start by inspecting the existing project structure before making any changes.

### 3.2 Indexes — `:529-545`
`donations(fund_id|date|status|donor_name)`, `expenses(date|category|status)`, `incomes(date)`, `members(status|full_name)`, `events(start_date|status)`, `announcements(status)`, `audit_logs(module|created_at)`, `prayer_times(date)`, `contact_requests(status)`.
Added later: `idx_donations_user_id` (`002:12`), `idx_members_user_id` (`003:6`).

### 3.3 Functions & Triggers
- `update_updated_at_column()` — `001:551-556`; applied as `set_updated_at BEFORE UPDATE` to 22 tables via a `DO` loop at `:558-570`. `event_members` and `contribution_reminder_emails` are not in that list (they have no `updated_at`).
- `update_fund_collected_amount()` — original `001:575`, **replaced twice**:
  - `005_fix_fund_collected_amount.sql`
  - `006_repair_fund_collected_amount.sql:11-70` — final version. Handles `DELETE` (`:14-24`), `INSERT` (`:26-36`), and `UPDATE` (`:38-66`) with `IS DISTINCT FROM` guards on `fund_id`, `amount`, `status`, `deleted_at`; subtract-then-add; `SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public, pg_temp` (`:70`). Trigger `trg_update_fund_amount AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OR DELETE ON donations` (`:72-75`). Backfill recomputes every fund from completed, non-deleted donations (`:78-86`). Rationale documented at `:1-9` (drift: General Fund stored 1,015,000 vs actual 15,999.82).
- `handle_new_user()` `001:603-611` + trigger `on_auth_user_created AFTER INSERT ON auth.users` (`:613-617`) — auto-creates `profiles` row.
- `handle_user_login()` `001:622-629` + trigger `on_auth_user_login AFTER INSERT ON auth.sessions` (`:630-634`) — updates `last_login`.
- `public.has_permission(text)` `001:640-661` — reads role from `profiles.role`, returns true for `super_admin`, else joins `user_roles`→`role_permissions`→`permissions`.
- `public.current_user_role()` `001:667-671` — `SELECT role FROM profiles WHERE id = auth.uid()`.

### 3.4 RLS
RLS is enabled on 26 tables (`001:676-701`). Policies by group:
- Public read: `mosque_settings` (`:709`), `prayer_times` (`:714`), `jummah_schedules` (`:720`), `announcements` published+in-window (`:726`), `events` published (`:733`), `khutbahs` published (`:740`), `committee_members` (`:747`), `donation_funds` `is_visible` (`:753`), `documents` `access_level='public'` (`:804`).
- Public write: `donations_submit` `WITH CHECK (true)` (`:760`), `contacts_public_write` `WITH CHECK (true)` (`:810`).
- Admin write policies follow the `has_permission(...) OR current_user_role() = 'super_admin'` pattern, one set per table (`:710-859`).
- Ownership: `profiles_own_read/update` via `auth.uid() = id`, `donations_own_read` via `auth.uid() = user_id` (`002:15-16`), `incomes_admin_*` allowing either `expense.*` or `donation.*`, `expenses_admin_update` additionally allowing `expense.approve` (`:775`), `audit_logs` restricted to `super_admin`/`admin` (`:832-833`), role/permission tables writable only by `super_admin` (`:845-859`).
- `supabase/recreate_admin_policies.sql` (114 lines) is a standalone script to drop/rebuild the admin policy block.

## 4. Auth & Session

- `src/proxy.ts` — exported `proxy` function, not `middleware`. Refreshes session (`:4-28`), redirects unauthenticated `/admin` → `/login`, authenticated `/login` → `/admin`, sets `x-pathname`; matcher at `:30-34`.
- `src/app/auth/callback/route.ts:4-18` — `code` → `exchangeCodeForSession` → redirect to `next` or `/admin`.
- `src/lib/supabase/{client,server,middleware,admin}.ts` — browser / cookie-bound server / middleware / service-role clients. `admin.ts:3-13` uses `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` with `auth: { persistSession: false }`.
- `src/lib/auth/session.ts` — `getCurrentUser()` (`:4-10`), `requireUser()` redirect guard (`:12-18`), `getCurrentProfile()` (`:20-34`).
- `src/lib/auth/actions.ts` — `loginAction` (`:15-54`: `signInWithPassword`, profile `last_login`/`status` update, audit entry, redirect `/admin`), `logoutAction` (`:56+`), plus password reset flow. Type `AuthActionState` is consumed by `src/app/(auth)/login/page.tsx:7-15` via `useActionState`.
- `(auth)/` group: `layout.tsx` is a pass-through fragment (`:1-7`); `login/page.tsx` is a client component; `forgot-password`, `reset-password`.
- DB triggers keep `profiles` and `last_login` in sync (§3.3).

## 5. RBAC — Database-Driven

- `src/lib/permissions.ts`
  - `SUPER_ADMIN`/`ADMIN` constants (`:1-2`), `isSuperAdminRole` (`:5-7`), `isAdminRole` (`:9-11`).
  - `NAV_PERMISSIONS` (`:17-46`) — one entry per admin route → required permission; `/admin/roles` is `kind: "super_admin"` (`:43`); `/admin/my-donations` uses `donation.view.own` with `excludedRoles: [super_admin, admin]` (`:19-23`).
  - `permissionsAllow()` (`:53-60`) — `"*"` wildcard for super admin.
  - `navItemAllowed()` (`:62-76`), `permissionForPath()` (`:79-92`, longest-prefix so nested routes inherit).
- `src/lib/access.ts` (`import "server-only"`)
  - `getPermissionsForRole()` (`:22-40`) — joins `role_permissions → permissions` with `roles!inner(name)`; super admin → `["*"]`; failures log and return `[]`.
  - `buildAccess()` (`:42-50`), `getCurrentAccess()` (`:53-58`).
  - Guards: `requirePermission` (`:64-70`, redirect `/admin/forbidden`), `requireSuperAdmin` (`:72-78`), `requireAdminRole` (`:80-86`), throwing variants `assertPermission` (`:89-95`), `assertSuperAdmin` (`:97-103`).
- `src/app/admin/layout.tsx:24-48` — requires auth + active profile, resolves permissions, renders `AdminShell` with `{ id, email, full_name, role }` and the permission list.
- 29 `requirePermission(...)` page guards across admin routes; `src/app/admin/forbidden/page.tsx` is the redirect target.
- Seed + migrations: `supabase/seed.sql:10-19` seeds roles `super_admin`, `admin`, `treasurer`, `imam`, `muazzin`, `committee_member`, `staff`, `member`. `004_muazzin_announcement_permission.sql:2-8` grants `announcement.manage` to `muazzin`. `007_permissions_referenced_by_code.sql` adds the missing `expense.delete` and `donation.view.own` permissions (`:20-23`), backfills `dashboard.view` for every role (`:26-31`), and restores `admin → expense.delete`, `member → donation.view.own` (`:35-41`). `008_permission_gated_admin_pages.sql` converts 11 role-name-only pages to real permissions using the `<module>.view` / `<module>.manage` convention (`:25-40+`, list at `:7-9`).

## 6. Server Actions — `src/lib/actions/admin.ts` (1852 lines, `"use server"`)

Shared helpers: `ensureUniqueSlug()` (`:37-51`, appends a 6-char uuid suffix), `getCurrentUserId()` (`:53-57`), `getCurrentUserRole()` (`:59-71`), `emptyToNull` (`:34-35`), `ActionResult` type (`:32`).

Pattern per mutation: `getCurrentAccess()` → `access.has("<perm>")` early-return → Zod parse → `createAdminClient()` or `createClient()` → mutate → `logAudit()` → `revalidatePath()`.

Donations: `createDonation` `:77`, `updateDonation` `:125`, `deleteDonation` `:169` (soft: `deleted_at`), `approveDonation` `:200`, `rejectDonation` `:230`.
Expenses: `createExpense` `:271`, `updateExpense` `:310`, `approveExpense` `:347`, `rejectExpense` `:377`, `deleteExpense` `:407`.
Income: `createIncome` `:439`, `updateIncome` `:476`, `deleteIncome` `:512`.
Funds: `createFund` `:543`, `updateFund` `:574`, `deleteFund` `:606`.
Members/committee/staff: `:621`, `:654`, `:677`; `:699`, `:728`, `:755`; `:769`, `:799`, `:825`.
Events: `createEvent` `:847`, `updateEvent` `:885`, `deleteEvent` `:922`.
Announcements `:941`, `:971`, `:1001`; Khutbah `:1019`, `:1048`, `:1077`; Assets `:1095`, `:1127`, `:1153`; Maintenance `:1171`, `:1204`, `:1234`; Documents `:1252`, `:1277`.
Contact requests `:1290`, `:1310`.
Prayer times: `upsertPrayerTimes` `:1328`, `copyPrayerTimes` `:1385`, `deletePrayerTimes` `:1443`.
Settings `updateSettings` `:1462`. Zakat `:1500`, `:1527`, `:1554`.
Admin identity: `createUserAccount` `:1585`, `updateUserRole` `:1686`, `toggleUserStatus` `:1716`, `saveRolePermissions` `:1751`, `syncUserRole` `:1835`.

`src/lib/actions/public.ts` (112 lines): `submitPublicDonation` `:13-70` — builds `raw` from `FormData`, validates with `donationSchema`, resolves the signed-in user (`:38-40`), mints `RCP-<ts>-<rand>` (`:42`), inserts with `status: "pending"`, `notes: "Submitted via public donation page"`, `user_id` (`:44-58`), revalidates `/donate` and returns the "JazakAllahu Khairan" confirmation (`:65-69`). `submitContactRequest` `:72`.

## 7. Domain Logic

### 7.1 Events → Fund Contributions (in-progress feature)
`src/lib/queries/admin.ts:601-699` is a self-contained contribution engine (all uncommitted):
- `getEventById` `:601-609` — event + joined `donation_funds`.
- `getEventMembers` `:611-619` — `event_members` + joined `members`.
- `getEventContributionRows` `:621-683` — `Promise.all` over `event_members`, `donations` filtered to `fund_id = event.fund_id AND status = 'completed' AND deleted_at IS NULL`, `contribution_reminder_emails`, and `members`. Groups donations by `member_id`, derives `assigned_amount` (falls back to `event.contribution_amount`), `paid_amount`, `remaining_amount`, and `status: 'completed' | 'incomplete'` (`:669-673`), plus `last_reminder`.
- `getEventContributionSummary` `:684-699` — totals, completed/incomplete counts, `completionPercent`.

Consequence worth knowing: because matching is by **fund**, any completed donation to the event's fund by a listed member counts toward that member's contribution, regardless of donation date or event linkage.

Supporting schema/types: `event_members` + `events.fund_id/contribution_*` + `donations.member_id` + `contribution_reminder_emails` in `001` (§3.1); `EventMember`, `EventMemberContribution`, `ContributionReminderEmail` types and `donationSchema.member_id`/`eventSchema` contribution fields + `eventMemberSchema`/`reminderEmailSchema` in `src/lib/validations/index.ts:155-168` and `src/types/database.ts:147-180`.

The admin UI has **not** been built yet: `src/app/admin/events/events-client.tsx:1-38` imports only `createEvent/updateEvent/deleteEvent`, `eventSchema`, and table/form components; `grep` for `contribution|getEventMembers` in `src/app/admin/events/` returns nothing.

### 7.2 Funds
`getFunds()` `queries/admin.ts:490`, `getVisibleFunds()` `queries/public.ts:269`, `getFundBySlug()` `public.ts:282`. `collected_amount` is never written by the app — only by the DB trigger (§3.3).

### 7.3 Members & Auth-Account Linking
`003_member_user_link.sql:4-6` adds `members.user_id`. `queries/admin.ts:360-427` builds a unified list: `memberFromMemberRow()` `:360`, `memberFromProfile()` `:383`, `buildMemberList()` `:406-427` — merges `members` with `profiles` of role `member`, skipping already-linked profiles and email matches, sorted newest first. `members-client.tsx:179` sets `user_id` on link, `:213` "Add Details", `:269` "Add Member Details" dialog title. `getMyDonations()` `queries/admin.ts:1081+` returns paginated donations plus a summed total for the current user.

### 7.4 Donations, Transactions, Approval- Public: `submitPublicDonation` always inserts `status: 'pending'`; the anon-key RLS policy `donations_submit WITH CHECK (true)` (`:760`) is what permits this. `receipt_number` is unique and generated server-side.
- Admin approval: `approveDonation` `actions/admin.ts:200-228` requires `donation.update`, sets `status: 'completed'` (which is what advances `donation_funds.collected_amount` via trigger), audits `action: "approve"`, revalidates `/admin/donations`, `/admin/funds`, `/admin`.
- Rejection: `rejectDonation` `:230-265` sets `status: 'cancelled'` and **appends the reason to `notes`** rather than using a dedicated column; revalidates the same three paths.
- UI: `src/app/admin/donations/donations-client.tsx:13-19` imports create/update/delete/approve/reject; approve handler at `:135`, success toast `:139`.
- Expenses use a different, richer flow: `expenses` has real `status`/`approved_by`/`approved_at`/`rejection_reason` columns; `approveExpense` `:347-375` requires `expense.approve` and stamps approver+timestamp; `rejectExpense` `:377-405` sets `status: 'rejected'` + `rejection_reason`; deletes are soft (`deleted_at`, `:407-433`).
- Reporting queries: `getDonations` `:214`, `getDonationById` `:259`, `getExpenses` `:269`, `getIncomes` `:316`, `getMonthlyFinancialSummary` `:1010`, `getExpenseByCategory` `:1055`, `getIncomeByCategory` `:1068`.

### 7.5 Other Domains
- Prayer times: `src/lib/prayer-times.ts` — mosque coords `23.7018, 90.3742` (`:13-14`), `addMinutesToTime` `:47`, `syncRealPrayerTimes(dates)` `:143`. Timezone helper `src/lib/utils/time-zone.ts:1` `MOSQUE_TIMEZONE = "Asia/Dhaka"`, `localDateInTimeZone` `:3`, `timePartsInTimeZone` `:15`.
- Audit: `src/lib/utils/audit.ts:12` `logAudit({ action, module, entity, entityId, oldData, newData })` → `audit_logs`; `src/lib/utils/ip.ts:3` `getClientIp()`.
- Formatting: `src/lib/utils/format.ts` — `cn` `:5`, `formatCurrency` (৳ default) `:9`, `formatDate` `:16`, `formatTime` `:26`, `slugify` `:56`, `getInitials` `:72`, `timeAgo` `:82`, `downloadCSV` `:102`, `getHijriDate` `:116`, `getNextPrayer` `:129`, `countdownToTime` `:155`.
- Validation: `src/lib/validations/index.ts` — Zod schema per entity (`donationSchema` `:51`, `expenseSchema`, `incomeSchema`, `fundSchema`, `memberSchema`, `committeeMemberSchema`, `staffSchema`, `eventSchema` `:136`, `eventMemberSchema` `:155`, `reminderEmailSchema` `:161`, `announcementSchema` `:171`, …) plus status/method constant arrays.

## 8. Email — `src/lib/email.ts` (untracked, 41 lines)

- Nodemailer transport at `:3-25` reading `SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_USER`, `SMTP_PASS`, `SMTP_SECURE`.
- `sendReminderEmail({ to, subject, html })` at `:27-41`, with `EMAIL_FROM_NAME` / `EMAIL_FROM` and fallbacks for `from`.
- **Zero callers.** `grep -rn "lib/email" src` returns nothing; `sendReminderEmail` appears only at its definition. `reminderEmailSchema` (`validations/index.ts:161`) and `contribution_reminder_emails` are likewise write-nowhere — only read in `queries/admin.ts:626-680`. The send action, its permission, and the events UI are still missing.
- `SMTP_*` / `EMAIL_FROM*` are absent from `.env.example`, `.env.local`, and `README.md:175-192`.

## 9. Admin UI System

- `src/components/admin/admin-shell.tsx:23` `AdminShell({ user, permissions, children })` — responsive layout (desktop collapse + mobile sheet).
- `src/components/admin/sidebar.tsx:150` `AdminSidebar({ collapsed, onNavigate, role, permissions })`; nav groups and24 items at `:62-115`; each filtered through `navItemAllowed`. Route labels for breadcrumbs live in `admin-header.tsx:42-67`; `Breadcrumbs` `:69-96`; `AdminHeader` `:98-183` with sidebar toggles, avatar dropdown, "View Site" link, conditional Settings entry (`canManageSettings` `:106`, `:160-167`), and `logoutAction()` on select (`:169-178`).
- Tables: `data-table.tsx` — `DataTable` `:29`, generic `Column<T>` (`:15-20`) and `DataTableProps<T>` (`:22-27`); dark-green header row (`:38`), empty state "No results." (`:50-58`), optional `onRowClick`.
- Responsive duplication: `mobile-record-card.tsx` exports `MobileRecordList` `:14`, `MobileRecordCard` `:33`, `MobileRecordHead` `:52`, `MobileMetaGrid` `:75`, `MobileMetaTile` `:94`, `MobileProgress` `:136`, `MobileRecordFooter` `:161`, `MobileActionButton` `:184`, `DesktopTableOnly` `:221` — used by funds, income, expenses, donations, khutbah, events, announcements, committee.
- Chrome: `filter-bar.tsx` (`FilterBarProps`/`Filter`/`FilterOption` `:78`), `pagination-bar.tsx` (`:141`), `table-wrapper.tsx` `AdminTableWrapper` (`:64`), `table-skeleton.tsx` (`:52`), `form-dialog.tsx` (`:53`), `page-actions.tsx` (`:37`), `status-badge.tsx` (`:56`), `dashboard.tsx` (`DashboardHero` `:58`, `StatsCard` `:158`, `MonthlyChart` `:240`, `DonationFundChart` `:282`, `RecentDonationsTable` `:342`, `RecentActivityTable` `:379`, `QuickActions` `:415`).
- Toasts: `sonner` throughout clients; global `Toaster` in `src/app/layout.tsx`.
- Server-component page + client-component split is the consistent convention: each admin route has `page.tsx` (permission guard + data fetch) and a `*-client.tsx` ("use client", React Hook Form + `useActionState`/`useTransition`).

## 10. Shared Forms & Primitives

`src/components/forms/`: `page-header.tsx:37`, `search-input.tsx:43`, `form-field.tsx:30`, `form-input.tsx:54`, `form-select.tsx:75` (`SelectOption`), `form-textarea.tsx:52`, `form-submit-button.tsx:39`, `confirm-dialog.tsx:79`, `empty-state.tsx:40`, `error-message.tsx:23`, barrel `index.ts`.
`src/components/ui/` (22 files, Radix + CVA): `button.tsx:53` (`buttonVariants`), `badge.tsx:36`, `card.tsx:57`, `table.tsx:83`, `dialog.tsx:92`, `dropdown-menu.tsx:147`, `select.tsx:115`, `sheet.tsx:104`, `avatar.tsx:41`, `alert.tsx:46`, `checkbox.tsx:25`, `input.tsx:18`, `label.tsx:24`, `pagination.tsx:90`, `popover.tsx:30`, `progress.tsx:25`, `separator.tsx:23`, `skeleton.tsx:12`, `switch.tsx:26`, `tabs.tsx:50`, `textarea.tsx:17`, `tooltip.tsx:29`.
`src/types/database.ts` holds hand-maintained row interfaces (`Profile` `:2-15`, `Event` `:124-146`, `EventMember`/`EventMemberContribution`/`ContributionReminderEmail` `:147-180`, `Donation` `:290+`).

## 11. Configuration & Environment

- `.env.example` (4 vars) and `.env.local` expose the same key names: `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`, `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`. Values were not read.
- Public queries use the anon client; admin mutations use the service-role client (`supabase/admin.ts:3-13`), which bypasses RLS — so **all** authorization for admin data is enforced in application code (`access.has(...)`) plus the admin layout guard, not by the database.
- `app/manifest.ts`, `app/robots.ts`, `app/sitemap.ts` for SEO/PWA. Font Awesome is used alongside Lucide in the public components.

## 12. Working Tree State (uncommitted work in progress)

`git status` on branch `master`:
- Modified: `package.json` (+nodemailer/@types), `package-lock.json`, `src/lib/queries/admin.ts` (+103), `src/lib/validations/index.ts` (+19), `src/types/database.ts` (+39), `supabase/migrations/001_initial_schema.sql` (+27).
- Untracked: `src/lib/email.ts`.
- Recent commits: `0edd51b` mobile card layouts, `9e8346d` "gate all admin pages on database permissions".

Together these are one coherent, incomplete feature: **event fund contributions with email reminders**. Schema, types, Zod schemas, and query layer exist; the server action, the admin UI, and the email wiring do not.

## 13. Findings & Risks

1. **`event_members` and `contribution_reminder_emails` have no RLS.** They are created at `001:181` and `001:330` but appear in neither the `ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` list (`001:676-701`) nor any policy — verified by `grep -rn` across all migrations, which finds only those two `CREATE TABLE` lines. On a live project with PostgREST exposed, these tables are readable by any authenticated client holding the anon key, leaking member/event/reminder-email data. Service-role writes bypass RLS anyway, so the fix is to add both tables to the enable list plus `event.manage`-gated policies.
2. **The two new tables were added to the already-applied `001_initial_schema.sql`.** `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` masks this on a fresh install, but an existing database will never receive them via `supabase db push` because `001` is recorded as applied. They need a new numbered migration.
3. **Email is entirely unwired**: `sendReminderEmail` has no caller, no SMTP vars are documented, and the SMTP block would throw when invoked without configuration.
4. **Contribution matching is fund-scoped, not event-scoped** (`queries/admin.ts:626-645`): any completed donation to the event's fund counts, so overlapping fund campaigns double-count members.
5. **Donation rejection loses structured data** — the reason is appended into `notes` (`actions/admin.ts:242-248`), unlike expenses which have `rejection_reason`.
6. **Service-role clients are used for admin data** (`actions/admin.ts:4`), so a missed `access.has()` check is a data-exposure bug rather than a permission denial; the `/admin/roles` editor changes permissions with effect on the next request, which is the intended design.
7. **`/admin/my-donations` is excluded for `super_admin` and `admin`** (`permissions.ts:22`) — deliberate, but worth confirming against expectations.
8. **Installed-but-unused deps**: `@tanstack/react-table`, most Radix packages, several FontAwesome packages.
9. `README.md:125` documents `lib/permissions/` as a directory; the actual files are `lib/permissions.ts` and `lib/access.ts`.
</task_result>
</task>

A modern, production-ready mosque management platform that combines a public-facing community website with a secure, role-based admin dashboard for managing operations, funding, events, and community members. 🏛️ Community Platform
Public website for mosque updates, prayer times, and announcements		 💰 Finance Tracking
Donation, expense, fund, and income management with reporting
👥 Member Management
Members, staff, committee, roles, and permission controls		 📊 Operational Insights
Reports, activity logs, and admin dashboards for decision making
## Why MMS? - Manage mosque operations from a single dashboard - Keep public content updated with announcements, prayer times, and events - Track donations, expenses, and funds with financial transparency - Handle members, staff, committee roles, and permissions cleanly - Maintain a professional digital presence for the community --- ## Features ### Public Website - Homepage with prayer times and next prayer countdown - Events and announcement sections - Khutbah archive and community content pages - Committee and gallery pages - Donation page with Bangladeshi Taka support - Contact page and public inquiry handling - SEO metadata, sitemap, robots configuration, and manifest support ### Admin Dashboard - Donation, income, expense, and balance overview - Charts for donation trends and fund allocation - Roles and permissions management - Members, committee, staff, and user controls - Prayer time management and operational records - Assets, maintenance, documents, and request workflows - Ramadan, audit logs, and settings modules ### Security & Access Control - Supabase authentication integration - Role-based access control (RBAC) - Permission checks enforced in logic and database policy layers - Secure server/client separation for sensitive operations --- ## Tech Stack | Layer | Technology | | --- | --- | | Frontend | Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript | | Styling | Tailwind CSS v4 | | UI Components | Radix UI, Lucide React | | Forms | React Hook Form, Zod | | Data Tables | TanStack Table | | Charts | Recharts | | Backend | Supabase (PostgreSQL, Auth, Storage, RLS) | | Notifications | Sonner | | Utilities | clsx, tailwind-merge, date-fns | --- ## Project Structure ```bash . ├── src/ │ ├── app/ │ │ ├── (public)/ # public-facing pages │ │ ├── (auth)/ # login and auth flows │ │ ├── admin/ # protected admin dashboard │ │ ├── api/ # API routes │ │ └── auth/ # OAuth/callback routes │ ├── components/ │ │ ├── admin/ # dashboard and admin UI │ │ ├── forms/ # reusable form components │ │ ├── public/ # public-facing UI │ │ └── ui/ # shadcn-style primitives │ ├── lib/ │ │ ├── actions/ # server actions │ │ ├── auth/ # auth helpers │ │ ├── queries/ # data fetchers │ │ ├── permissions/ # RBAC rules │ │ ├── supabase/ # Supabase clients │ │ ├── utils/ # formatting and helpers │ │ ├── validations/ # Zod schemas │ │ └── prayer-times.ts # time-related logic │ ├── constants/ │ ├── types/ │ └── proxy.ts # proxy/middleware replacement for Next 16 ├── supabase/ │ ├── migrations/ │ └── seed.sql ├── public/ ├── package.json ├── next.config.ts ├── tsconfig.json ├── eslint.config.mjs ├── README.md └── .env.example ``` --- ## Getting Started ### Prerequisites - Node.js 18.18+ (recommended: Node 20 LTS) - A Supabase project - A configured local environment for development ### Installation ```bash npm install ``` ### Run the app ```bash npm run dev ``` Then open: ```text http://localhost:3000 ``` --- ## Environment Variables Create a `.env.local` file in the project root using the following values: ```env NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=https://your-project.supabase.co NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=your-anon-key SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=your-service-role-key NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=http://localhost:3000 ``` ### Variable Notes - `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`: Your Supabase project URL - `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`: Public anon key for browser access - `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`: Server-side secret; keep it private - `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`: Base URL used by the app in local or production environments --- ## Database Setup Apply the database schema and policies from the Supabase migrations. ```bash # If you use the Supabase CLI supabase db push ``` Or import the SQL files manually from the `supabase/migrations/` directory in the Supabase SQL editor. Then seed initial data using: ```bash supabase/seed.sql ``` This file contains initial records such as roles, funds, and default system data. For the first admin user, create the account in the Supabase Auth dashboard and update the corresponding profile record to assign the appropriate role, such as `super_admin`. --- ## Available Scripts ```bash npm run dev # start development server npm run build # production build npm run start # run production build npm run lint # run ESLint ``` --- ## Notes - Currency is handled in Bangladeshi Taka (`৳`) - The donation flow is designed for manual payment tracking rather than a third-party payment gateway - This project uses modern Next.js conventions; in Next 16, the role of middleware is handled through the app proxy setup in `src/proxy.ts` --- ## Contributing Contributions are welcome. If you want to improve the application, please open an issue or submit a pull request with a clear description of the change. --- ## Project Status This project is under active development and is designed for mosque administration workflows, community engagement, and operational reporting.

Excellent, the exploration is very thorough. Key finding: there's already substantial WIP:
- `001_initial_schema.sql` has `event_members`, `contribution_reminder_emails`, `events.fund_id`, `events.contribution_amount`, `contribution_start_date`, `contribution_due_date`
- `donations.member_id` exists
- `src/lib/queries/admin.ts:601-699` has contribution query functions
- `src/types/database.ts` has `EventMember`, `EventMemberContribution`, `ContributionReminderEmail`
- `src/lib/validations/index.ts` has `eventMemberSchema`, `reminderEmailSchema`
- `src/lib/email.ts` exists with nodemailer but zero callers

Missing:
1. A new migration for existing DBs (event_members, contribution_reminder_emails + RLS)

-- ============================================================
-- EVENT CONTRIBUTION TRACKING
-- ============================================================
-- `events.fund_id`, `events.contribution_*`, `event_members` and
-- `contribution_reminder_emails` were appended to 001 after that migration had
-- already been applied to live databases, so an existing project would never
-- pick them up through the normal migration chain. Everything below is
-- idempotent: it is a no-op on a fresh install (001 already created the
-- objects) and creates whatever is missing everywhere else.
--
-- Design note: no duplicate money is stored here. `event_members.assigned_amount`
-- is the only new amount, and it is a target, not a ledger. Collected totals,
-- paid amounts and Completed/Incomplete status are always derived from approved
-- `donations` rows (status = 'completed') that carry `donations.member_id`.

-- ============================================================
-- COLUMNS
-- ============================================================

ALTER TABLE events
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS fund_id UUID REFERENCES donation_funds(id) ON DELETE SET NULL;

ALTER TABLE events
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS contribution_amount NUMERIC(12,2) DEFAULT 0;

ALTER TABLE events
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS contribution_start_date DATE;

ALTER TABLE events
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS contribution_due_date DATE;

-- ============================================================
-- TABLES
-- ============================================================

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS event_members (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuid_generate_v4(),
  event_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES events(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  member_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES members(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  assigned_amount NUMERIC(12,2) DEFAULT 0,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
  created_by UUID REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  UNIQUE (event_id, member_id)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS contribution_reminder_emails (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuid_generate_v4(),
  event_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES events(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  member_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES members(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  recipient_email TEXT NOT NULL,
  subject TEXT NOT NULL,
  message TEXT NOT NULL,
  sent_by UUID REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  sent_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
  status VARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'sent' CHECK (status IN ('sent','failed'))
);

-- `donations.member_id` is the link that makes payment -> member matching a
-- foreign key lookup instead of name/email/phone string guessing. Backfill it
-- from the donor's own account where a member row clearly belongs to them, but
-- only when there is exactly one plausible member so nothing is guessed wrong.
UPDATE donations d
SET member_id = m.user_id_link
FROM (
  SELECT p.id AS user_id_link, p.email
  FROM profiles p
  WHERE p.role = 'member' AND p.email IS NOT NULL
) m
WHERE d.member_id IS NULL
  AND d.user_id IS NOT NULL
  AND d.member_id = m.user_id_link;

-- ============================================================
-- INDEXES
-- ============================================================

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_event_members_event_id ON event_members(event_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_event_members_member_id ON event_members(member_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_contribution_reminder_emails_event_id
  ON contribution_reminder_emails(event_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_contribution_reminder_emails_member_id
  ON contribution_reminder_emails(member_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_events_fund_id ON events(fund_id);

-- ============================================================
-- ROW LEVEL SECURITY
-- ============================================================
-- These two tables were created without RLS in 001, which left them readable by
-- any client holding the anon key. Members' names, phones, emails and the full
-- reminder history all live here, so both are locked down behind `event.manage`.

ALTER TABLE event_members ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
ALTER TABLE contribution_reminder_emails ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

DROP POLICY IF EXISTS event_members_admin_all ON event_members;
CREATE POLICY event_members_admin_all ON event_members
  FOR ALL
  USING (public.has_permission('event.manage') OR public.current_user_role() = 'super_admin')
  WITH CHECK (public.has_permission('event.manage') OR public.current_user_role() = 'super_admin');

DROP POLICY IF EXISTS contribution_reminder_emails_admin_all ON contribution_reminder_emails;
CREATE POLICY contribution_reminder_emails_admin_all ON contribution_reminder_emails
  FOR ALL
  USING (public.has_permission('event.manage') OR public.current_user_role() = 'super_admin')
  WITH CHECK (public.has_permission('event.manage') OR public.current_user_role() = 'super_admin');

-- No public read policy on purpose: contribution status is financial member data.

-- `donations.member_id` is the link that makes payment -> member matching a
-- foreign key lookup instead of name/email/phone string guessing. Backfill it
-- from the donor's own account where a member row clearly belongs to them, but
-- only when there is exactly one plausible member so nothing is guessed wrong.
UPDATE donations d
SET member_id = m.user_id_link
FROM (
  SELECT p.id AS user_id_link, p.email
  FROM profiles p

input.newString:
-- `donations.member_id` is the link that makes payment -> member matching a
-- foreign key lookup instead of name/email/phone string guessing (003 added
-- `members.user_id`). Backfill the gap for donations that carry a `user_id` but
-- no `member_id`, matching on that account link only -- never on a name. The
-- correlated subquery keeps this to one row per donation even if a user somehow
-- owns several member records.
UPDATE donations d
SET member_id = (
  SELECT m.id
  FROM members m
  WHERE m.user_id = d.user_id
  ORDER BY m.created_at
  LIMIT 1
)
WHERE d.member_id IS NULL
  AND d.user_id IS NOT NULL
  AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM members m WHERE m.user_id = d.user_id);

Since I already fetch all completed donations for the fund in `getEventContributionRows`, I can compute `fundCollected` = sum of ALL completed donations for the fund (including donations from non-assigned members and without member_id). That's exactly right and matches requirement 6/29: "Progress must come from approved payments only" and "use approved fund contributions as the financial source of truth".

   Important nuance: `totalPaid` from rows only counts assigned members' donations. `fundCollected` counts all. The summary card "Collected" should be the fund collected (source of truth = fund). And "Target Collection" should be... the event target. Requirement 38 says expected = memberCount × perHead, and to show the difference vs the Fund target without overwriting. I'll show the event expected as the headline target and surface fund target in the mismatch banner. Actually let me think about which is more correct for the "Target Collection" card.

Now the server actions. Let me add them to `src/lib/actions/admin.ts` after the event section. I need:

1. `addEventMembers(formData)` — takes event_id, member_ids (repeated), optional assigned_amount. Uses admin client, upsert to ignore conflicts, audit.
2. `removeEventMember(formData)` — delete event_members row, audit.
3. `updateEventMemberAmount(formData)` — update assigned_amount, audit.
4. `sendContributionReminder(prevState, formData)` — the email action. Needs to:
   - check `event.manage`
   - validate with reminderEmailSchema
   - **resolve the recipient email from the member profile server-side**, not trust the form (spec 15: "must come automatically from the Member profile. Do not require Admin to manually type"). So the action should ignore form-provided recipient_email and read `members.email`. I'll validate the member has an email. I'll still keep the field in the schema shape but override from DB. Actually cleaner: don't accept recipient_email at all in the form; derive it. But schema requires it. Let me pass the derived email into safeParse after fetching the member. That way schema still validates email format and form tampering is impossible.
   - fetch event + member
   - compute assigned/paid/remaining — should be derived server-side, not from form. Let me reuse `getEventContributionRows` and find the row. That guarantees the numbers in the email match the table. 
   - fetch mosque settings for name/logo/address/phone
   - build subject/message/html; message from form (admin editable), subject from form (admin editable)
   - send, on success insert `contribution_reminder_emails` with status 'sent'
   - on failure, insert with status 'failed' and return error without internals
   - audit 'reminder_sent'
   - revalidatePath(`/admin/events/${eventId}`)

   Wait — the message field: spec 17 says pre-fill with a professional default message, admin can edit. So the client sends the (possibly edited) message. Good. But I want the message body itself to include the amount summary. My `buildReminderMessage` includes the amounts plus the admin message. Hmm — if admin edits the "message" textarea, and that textarea is prefilled with the full default message (including amounts), then appending it again would duplicate.

   Let me restructure: the modal's textarea is prefilled with just the *body prose* (the friendly-reminder paragraph), not the full default email. Then the server composes: greeting + event line + amounts + admin message + sign-off. That's cleaner and matches the HTML template structure where the admin message is a distinct block.

   But spec 17's example shows the whole thing in one textarea. Hmm. If the whole thing is in one textarea, then the amounts shown in the card are informational and the email body is fully admin-controlled. That's actually more faithful to the spec AND simpler/more predictable: what admin sees = what gets sent.

   Decision: the textarea holds the **full message body** (greeting → sign-off), prefilled from `buildReminderMessage`. The server sends `message` as the plain-text body verbatim, and renders the HTML template using the structured details (amounts/due date from DB) plus the admin message verbatim as the message block. This means the admin message appears once in HTML (inside the styled block) and once in the text part.

   Hmm, but then in the HTML the greeting would appear twice (template greeting + admin message greeting). Slightly redundant.

   Better: make `buildReminderHtml` accept the admin message and render it as the body block, where the admin message IS the full body text. So the HTML becomes: header → member name greeting (template) → event line (template) → amounts table (template) → admin message block (verbatim, which itself begins with "Assalamu Alaikum ...") → footer.

   That reads fine actually: greeting, then reminder line, then amount table, then the admin's written message (which opens with the greeting), then footer. Slightly repetitive greeting but perfectly normal for a real email, and the admin controls it.

   To keep it tidy, I'll prefill the admin message with just the prose paragraph (without greeting/sign-off), which is the more useful editing surface — spec says "Pre-fill it with a professional default message. Example concept: Assalamu Alaikum [Member Name] ...". The example includes greeting. 

   I'll go with: prefill = full default (greeting + body + sign-off) as spec'd. In the HTML, render the admin message as the body block. It's faithful and predictable. Done deliberating.

   One more consideration: to avoid double greeting in HTML, I'll render the greeting inside the message block only if the message starts with "Assalamu" — no, too clever. Keep it simple and just render the block.

```env
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=https://your-project.supabase.co
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=your-anon-key
SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=your-service-role-key
NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=http://localhost:3000
```

### Variable Notes

- `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`: Your Supabase project URL
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`: Public anon key for browser access
- `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`: Server-side secret; keep it private
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`: Base URL used by the app in local or production environments

### Email (Event Contribution Reminders)

Reminders are sent from the server with Nodemailer over SMTP. These variables are optional:
without them the contribution tracking page still works, it just reports that reminders are
disabled and the send button stays unavailable.

```env
SMTP_HOST=smtp.example.com
SMTP_PORT=587
SMTP_USER=your-smtp-username
SMTP_PASS=your-smtp-password
SMTP_SECURE=false
EMAIL_FROM=admin@your-mosque.com
EMAIL_FROM_NAME=Al-Noor Mosque
```

- `SMTP_PORT`: `587` for STARTTLS, `465` for implicit TLS (`SMTP_SECURE=true` is applied automatically on 465)
- `EMAIL_FROM`: must be an address the provider accepts as a verified sender. It always falls back to `SMTP_USER` if omitted, and can never be set from the browser
- These values are read only in `src/lib/email.ts`, which is a `server-only` module, so credentials never reach client code

- Ramadan, audit logs, and settings modules

### Event Contribution Tracking

An event can be linked to an existing donation fund and given a per-head contribution amount.
Members are then assigned to the event, and the linked fund's approved payments drive everything
on the event's contribution page (`/admin/events/<eventId>`):

```
Approved Fund Contribution  →  donations.member_id identifies the member
                           →  paid / remaining derived at render time
                           →  Completed / Incomplete derived (paid >= assigned)
                           →  summary counts and progress bar follow automatically
```

- Per-member assigned, paid, remaining, and Completed/Incomplete status
- Search, status and payment-stage filters, sorting, and pagination
- Email reminders to one member at a time, with history of what was sent and when
- No second payment system: approving a donation in `/admin/donations` is all it takes

### Security & Access Control

parts.text:
Done. The feature is built as a tracking layer on top of your existing fund system — no rebuild, no second payment system.

## What I found first

Your repo already had an **incomplete version** of this feature: the `event_members` and `contribution_reminder_emails` tables, the contribution query functions, Zod schemas, types, and an unused nodemailer lib. Missing were the server actions, the entire UI, and — importantly — a way to actually get those tables onto a live database.

## Two real bugs I fixed along the way

1. **`001_initial_schema.sql` was already applied**, so the two new tables would never reach your database. Added `supabase/migrations/009_event_contributions.sql` (idempotent — safe on fresh and existing installs).
2. **Both new tables had RLS enabled on26 others but not these two** — any client with the anon key could read member names, phones, emails and the full reminder history. Migration 009 locks them behind `event.manage`.

I also caught that empty date fields would have thrown on the `DATE` column insert, and empty number inputs produced `NaN` that failed validation confusingly.

## How the money stays truthful

`donations.member_id` already existed (migration 002), so payment→member matching is a foreign-key lookup, not name/email guessing. All figures derive at render time in one pure function (`src/lib/utils/contribution.ts`) — status is never stored. Approving a donation in `/admin/donations` is the only action needed; the event page follows.

I verified the spec's test scenario by compiling and running the real derivation function — **10/10 passed**, including Rahim (৳520 → Completed), Karim's partial (৳300 → remaining ৳220 → Incomplete, then auto-completes at ৳520), and overpayment (৳600 → remaining clamped to ৳0, actual paid preserved).

## Security choices worth flagging

The reminder action **re-derives** the recipient address and all three amounts server-side from the member row — the form only carries subject and wording. A tampered form can't redirect the mail or leak another member's figures. Send failures record a `failed` row and return a generic message; transport errors go to the server log only.

The sender address comes solely from `EMAIL_FROM`/`SMTP_USER` — never request data, so it can't be spoofed. `src/lib/email.ts` is `server-only`, and I confirmed no client component references SMTP or env vars.

## Two decisions you may want to overrule

- **Sorting/filtering/pagination run client-side** on the already-materialized row set rather than round-tripping to Postgres per keystroke. Correct at your scale (500 members ≈ 100KB); worth revisiting past a few thousand.
- **Contribution matching is fund-scoped**, matching your existing design. If two events share one fund, payments count toward both. Fine for one fund per event; flag it if you plan to share funds.

Bulk reminders are deliberately not built — `sendContributionReminder` is already single-recipient and non-looping, so "Remind All Incomplete" is a straightforward follow-up.

`tsc` clean, build clean, lint at 0 errors (37 warnings, down from the 41 baseline). Run `supabase db push` or paste migration 009 into the SQL editor before testing.

## Important Details
- Approved payments in this codebase are `donations.status = "completed"`.
- Payment-to-member matching uses `donations.member_id`; no name/email/phone guessing.
- Financial values are derived:
  - `paid_amount` = approved donations for the event’s linked fund and member.
  - `remaining_amount = max(assigned_amount - paid_amount, 0)`.
  - `completed` when paid amount covers assignment; otherwise `incomplete`.
- No duplicate `event_collected_amount` or manually toggled status is stored.
- `event.manage` gates event contribution pages, assignments, removal, reminder sending, and the assignable-members API; seed grants it to `admin` and `treasurer`.

- `donations.member_id` exists through migration `002_donation_member_history.sql`; `members.user_id` exists through `003_member_user_link.sql`.
- Rows are fully derived server-side, then searched/sorted/filtered/paginated client-side; `/admin/events/[eventId]` is `force-dynamic`.

1: /**
2:  * Shared reminder copy for contribution emails.
3:  *
4:  * Deliberately free of any `server-only` import so the admin form can prefill the
5:  * subject and message with exactly what the server will send. Keeping a single
6:  * implementation means the modal can never show one wording and mail another.
7:  */
8: 
9: export type ReminderDetails = {
10:   memberName: string;
11:   eventName: string;
12:   assignedAmount: number;
13:   paidAmount: number;
14:   remainingAmount: number;
15:   dueDate: string | null;
16:   mosqueName: string;
17: };
18: 
19: export function formatTaka(amount: number) {
20:   return `৳${Number(amount || 0).toLocaleString("en-US", {
21:     minimumFractionDigits: 0,
22:     maximumFractionDigits: 2,
23:   })}`;
24: }
25: 
26: export function formatReminderDueDate(value: string | null | undefined) {
27:   if (!value) return "the scheduled date";
28:   const parsed = new Date(value);
29:   if (Number.isNaN(parsed.getTime())) return value;
30:   return parsed.toLocaleDateString("en-GB", {
31:     day: "numeric",
32:     month: "long",
33:     year: "numeric",
34:     timeZone: "UTC",
35:   });
36: }
37: 
38: export function buildReminderSubject(eventName: string, mosqueName: string) {
39:   return `Contribution Reminder - ${eventName} | ${mosqueName}`;
40: }
41: 
42: /** Default message body. The admin can edit any part of it before sending. */
43: export function buildReminderMessage(details: ReminderDetails) {
44:   const { memberName, eventName, mosqueName } = details;
45: 
46:   return [
47:     `Assalamu Alaikum ${memberName},`,
48:     "",
49:     `This is a friendly reminder regarding your contribution for "${eventName}" organised by ${mosqueName}.`,
50:     "",
51:     `Assigned Contribution: ${formatTaka(details.assignedAmount)}`,
52:     `Paid: ${formatTaka(details.paidAmount)}`,
53:     `Remaining: ${formatTaka(details.remainingAmount)}`,
54:     `Due Date: ${formatReminderDueDate(details.dueDate)}`,
55:     "",
56:     "We would appreciate your contribution within the scheduled period.",
57:     "",
58:     "JazakAllahu Khairan.",
59:     mosqueName,
60:   ].join("\n");
61: }
